nodes.label: Bug Report Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Structured intake form (title prefix '[Bug] ', auto-label 'bug') so reports arrive with description, reproduction steps, expected behaviour, screenshots and version data already filled in, reducing triage round-trips.

nodes.label: Required Version Triple (Minecraft / Fabric Loader / Mod)
nodes.rationale: A ColourScroller build is only meaningful as a (Minecraft version, Fabric Loader version, mod version) tuple because the mod is compiled per-MC-version; the template's placeholders (1.21.5 / 0.17.3 / 1.0.0) mirror the shipped 1.0.0 build exactly.
nodes.norm_label: required version triple (minecraft / fabric loader / mod)

nodes.label: Feature Request Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Titled '[Feature] ' and auto-labelled 'enhancement'; asks for the underlying problem before the proposed solution so requests can be evaluated against the roadmap rather than implemented literally. Collects only the Minecraft version, since feature scope is not loader-specific.

nodes.label: Publish on GitHub with version (Workflow)
nodes.rationale: Manually triggered (workflow_dispatch only) rather than on push/tag, because the release version is derived from the branch/ref name being dispatched — the maintainer picks which per-Minecraft-version branch to cut a release from.

nodes.label: build Job (ubuntu-latest)
nodes.rationale: Checks out with submodules: true and requests contents: write so the same job can build the artifact and create the GitHub release without a second job or elevated PAT.

nodes.label: Gradle clean build Step
nodes.rationale: Runs ./gradlew clean build after a conditional chmod +x guarded by runner.os != 'Windows', so the workflow stays portable if the runner is ever switched to a Windows image.

nodes.label: Java 21 Temurin Toolchain
nodes.rationale: JAVA_VERSION=21 is declared as a job-level env var and also hardcoded in setup-java; the env var exists so the same value can be forwarded to mc-publish as release metadata. Java 21 is the runtime baseline for Minecraft 1.21.x.

nodes.label: Release Version Scheme (1.0.0-mc.<MC_VERSION>)
nodes.rationale: MC_VERSION is taken from github.ref_name, so releases are cut from per-Minecraft-version branches (e.g. 1.21.11) and encode the target game version in the tag. The mod version '1.0.0' is hardcoded in the shell step rather than read from gradle.properties, so it must be edited by hand for every release — a drift hazard against CHANGELOG.md and README.md.

nodes.label: mc-publish Release Action
nodes.rationale: Kir-Antipov/mc-publish@v3.3.0 is configured with only github-tag/github-token, so it publishes to GitHub Releases alone even though the same action can target Modrinth and CurseForge; loaders is pinned to fabric and game-versions to the branch-derived MC version.

nodes.label: ColourScroller 1.0.0 Release (MC 1.21.5)
nodes.rationale: Promotes the mod from alpha to a 1.0.0 release alongside the 1.21.5 target bump; bundles toolchain updates (mod loader 0.17.3, Loom 1.13-SNAPSHOT, Gradle 8.14) with feature work (more scrollable blocks, unbindable base key, icon) and a mixin/class refactor plus removal of dead files.

nodes.label: Unbindable Base Key Option
nodes.rationale: Allowing the base modifier key to be unbound makes the chord optional, so users who dislike two-key combos can trigger Scroll Row / Scroll Single directly with the mouse wheel.

nodes.label: Class and Mixin Refactor
nodes.rationale: Mixins are the Fabric injection mechanism used to intercept scroll input; the 1.0.0 refactor reorganised these classes and deleted unnecessary files as part of leaving alpha.

nodes.label: ColourScroller (Fabric Mod)
nodes.rationale: A Fabric mod for fast in-game cycling of item colour/type variants, either for a single held stack or across a whole hotbar row. MIT licensed; a maintained fork of Anware-Canella's original, built from a concept by Sergent_Patate.

nodes.label: FabricAPI Requirement
nodes.rationale: Hard runtime dependency — the mod uses Fabric API for key-binding registration and client-tick hooks, so it will not function without it.

nodes.label: Client-Side, Creative-Mode-Only Constraint
nodes.rationale: Swapping a held stack for a different variant requires creative-mode item creation, which the client can request directly; this keeps the mod purely client-side (no server install, no protocol changes) at the cost of not working in survival.

nodes.label: Scroll Single
nodes.rationale: Cycles only the selected stack through its variant chain (e.g. white wool -> light gray wool -> gray wool) while deliberately preserving NBT and stack count, so the swap is non-destructive to enchantments/custom data and does not reset the stack size.

nodes.label: Scroll Row
nodes.rationale: Advances every scrollable item in the hotbar by one step per scroll tick regardless of which list each item belongs to, so a palette of wool + stained glass + concrete can be recoloured together in one gesture.

nodes.label: Cross-List Synchronization Toggle
nodes.rationale: Solves the unequal-list-length problem in Scroll Row. Sync ON makes the longest hotbar list dictate the cycle: all lists advance independently until the longest would wrap, at which point every item snaps back to its own first entry, skipping the tail of shorter lists so the whole hotbar realigns each pass. Sync OFF (the default) advances each list modulo its own size, so lists never realign — chosen as default because independent stepping is less surprising and never silently skips entries.

nodes.label: Scrollable Set (Variant List)
nodes.rationale: The core data structure: a named, ordered list of items forming one family (wool, stained glass, concrete, walls/slabs/stairs). Order defines the cycle sequence, which is why the editor exposes Move Left / Move Right; sets are user-editable rather than hardcoded so new block families can be added without a mod update.

nodes.label: In-Game Set Editor
nodes.rationale: Runtime GUI (default key K) for creating, renaming, reordering and deleting scrollable sets. Save & Apply writes to disk and applies immediately with no restart; Reload File discards local edits, Cancel discards without saving. Shift-click in the item picker adds multiple items without closing it. Known rough edge: Reload Default Sets wipes all user sets without confirmation.

nodes.label: ColourScroller/config/colourscroller.json
nodes.rationale: On-disk persistence for scrollable sets, written by the editor's Save & Apply. Shipping a JSON config (delivered in 1.0.2) was the first step of the user-editable-lists roadmap item before the 1.1.0 GUI made hand-editing optional; users are asked to attach this file to bug reports.

nodes.label: Base Key Binding (Left Ctrl)
nodes.rationale: Modifier held alongside Scroll Row / Scroll Single to arm scrolling, preventing accidental variant swaps during normal play. Optional: if left unbound the action keys work on their own.

nodes.label: Open Set Editor Key Binding (K)
nodes.rationale: Dedicated key opening the set editor in-game, so set management does not require alt-tabbing to the config file.

nodes.label: Planned Survival Mode Support
nodes.rationale: Outstanding roadmap item: instead of conjuring the next variant, pick the next item in the set that already exists in the player's inventory — the only design that can work without creative-mode item creation. Explicitly time-boxed by the maintainer being a university student working on this in free time.

nodes.label: Original colourscroller by Anware-Canella
nodes.rationale: Upstream project this repository descends from (github.com/Anware-Canella/colourscroller).

nodes.label: ColourScroller fork by TheMisterFish
nodes.rationale: Intermediate maintainer/fork in the lineage between the original project and this repository.

nodes.label: Sergent_Patate (Concept Author)
nodes.rationale: Credited with the original concept for the mod; his YouTube demo video documents the first version, predating the set editor and sync toggle.
